history: The Honda Civic Type R represents the ultimate expression of Honda's engineering philosophy — maximum performance through precision engineering rather than raw displacement. The FK8 generation, launched in North America for 2017, marked the first time Honda officially brought the legendary Type R badge stateside, and it arrived with a statement: a Nürburgring lap record for front-wheel-drive production cars.

Powering the Type R is Honda's K20C1 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder, producing 316 horsepower and 295 lb-ft of torque. Unlike many turbocharged engines that sacrifice high-rpm excitement for low-end torque, the K20C1 pulls strongly all the way to its 7,000 rpm redline — a hallmark of Honda's VTEC-influenced engineering DNA.

The Type R's chassis is equally impressive. Honda's dual-axis strut front suspension virtually eliminates torque steer — the arch-enemy of powerful front-wheel-drive cars — allowing the driver to put down power aggressively mid-corner without the wheel fighting back. The standard limited-slip differential further enhances traction out of corners.

The FL5 generation arrived for 2023 with a more mature design, revised suspension tuning, and a further refined powertrain. While critics initially questioned the controversial styling of the FK8, the driving experience was beyond reproach — setting yet another Nürburgring front-wheel-drive production car record and cementing the Type R's legacy as the benchmark hot hatch.
did_you_know: The FK8 Civic Type R set the Nürburgring Nordschleife lap record for front-wheel-drive production cars in 2017 with a time of 7:43.80 — beating the previous record held by the Volkswagen Golf GTI Clubsport S by over two seconds. It then broke its own record with the FL5 in 2023.

trims.name: Civic Type R
trims.description: The sole trim level for the FK8 generation — Honda's one-size-fits-all approach ensures every Type R buyer gets the full package: Brembo brakes, adaptive dampers, LSD, and the full aero kit.

trims.name: Type R (FL5)
trims.description: The redesigned FL5 generation with a more mature exterior, revised suspension geometry, and a 2.0L turbo producing the same 315 hp but with improved throttle response and a more linear power delivery.

trims.name: Type R Touring
trims.description: FL5-exclusive trim adding a premium Bose audio system, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and additional interior comfort features while retaining the complete performance hardware.

trims.name: Limited Edition
trims.description: Final-year FK8 special edition in Championship White only, featuring bronze BBS wheels, red brake calipers, and an Alcantara interior — a send-off to the generation that put the Type R on the American map.

variants.name: FK8 Limited Edition
variants.description: The swan song of the FK8 generation, limited to 100 units in the US. Championship White with bronze BBS forged wheels and red Brembo calipers made it instantly recognizable — and immediately collectible.

variants.name: Mugen Civic Type R
variants.description: Honda's in-house tuning arm Mugen offered a comprehensive upgrade package for the FK8 including a Mugen exhaust, carbon fiber aero additions, and suspension tuning. A Japan-market favorite widely imported by enthusiasts.

variants.name: FL5 Type R
variants.description: The 2023 FL5 generation refined everything the FK8 did well. A more grown-up design, better everyday livability, and another Nürburgring record made it the definitive modern Type R — and arguably the best front-wheel-drive car ever made.
